analysis:
Two small, API-adaptation-style changes were examined.

1) EngineV2VLMTextExtraction.swift lines 166, 258 and 264: `reKeyedQwenTargetWeights` is now `throws` and calls `try sanitizer.sanitize(weights:)`. The call site at line 166 uses `try`, and `extractQwen35` already throws. All errors land in the existing factory catch, which produces the `engine_v2_refusal` load failure. This is fail-closed: a sanitizer failure now propagates instead of being swallowed. The filtering to the `language_model.` prefix, the exclusion of `mtp.*` and vision weights, the strict `update(verify: [.all])`, and the parity gate are all unchanged. No new trust boundary or data exposure.

2) MediaIngest.swift line 422: `if case .ciImage(let ci) = image` became `image.source`. This presumably follows an upstream MLXLMCommon change in which `UserInput.Image` wraps a source enum. It is the aggregate-pixel reconciliation for nil-header images, a decompression-bomb guard. The pre-decode header charge at lines 407-415 and the per-image cap and extent backstop in `decodeImageData` (lines 721 and 751-755) remain intact. If `image.source` did not match the `.ciImage` case, the post-decode aggregate recheck would be silently skipped. The base `decodeImageData` returns `.ciImage(image)`, which suggests the change tracks a dependency API. The dependency (MLXLMCommon `UserInput.Image.source`) is not in the supplied evidence, so I cannot confirm that `decodeImageData`'s `.ciImage` return value still maps to `.source` as `.ciImage`. Nothing indicates a regression, but the fix depends on that external contract. Relevant threats: T-050 (media handling) and the availability posture of TB-007. No findings; a modest review of the dependency bump is advisable.
